clue.text: Training area for road users?

parts.note: read as a place where trains meet road traffic, not a driving school for motorists

explanation.surface: Sounds like a practice ground where learner drivers are taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' wants to mean teaching; here it is trains running, at the spot where a railway crosses a road on the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line crossing a road at grade is a place where trains and road vehicles share space.

clue.text: Pub landlord in council administration?

definitions.meaning: the person in charge of your local, the neighbourhood pub, is jokingly its boss
the body of elected councillors running a town or county

explanation.surface: A publican is drafted into running the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is British slang for a regular neighbourhood pub, so its landlord is humorously the authority there.
explanation.definitionFit: The official term for a district or county council in Britain is this phrase, the body that governs a locality.

clue.text: Containers routed through Largs when empty

parts.note: travelling via a place means being routed through it

indicators.note: a word emptied of its insides keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bottles being shipped by way of Largs, a Scottish seaside town, arrive with nothing in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass bottles for medicine or perfume are a kind of container.

clue.text: Prospects of lights on projections at sea

parts.note: to light on something is to alight or settle there, so lights means lands
headlands jutting out into the sea are capes

explanation.surface: Beacons shining from headlands give a view across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' looks like a noun (lamps); it is the verb, to come down on, as a bird lights on a branch. In a down clue 'on' simply puts one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect in the sense of a wide view of scenery is the same as a vista of countryside.

clue.text: Become aware of true side deceptive daughter's hidden

parts.note: something true is real

indicators.note: deceptive suggests the word side is not what it seems, so its letters are rearranged
the daughter is hidden away, meaning taken out of the shuffled letters

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up to the fact that a lying daughter's real side has been concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deceptive daughter' reads as a lying girl, but 'deceptive' is the anagram signal and 'hidden' means the daughter's letter is removed before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp or come to understand a fact is to become conscious of it.

clue.text: Split up FBI agents in group

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the word for a group

parts.note: a set is a group of things
G-men is American slang for FBI agents (government men)

explanation.surface: A gang of FBI agents is broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to divide something into parts or sections is to break it apart.

clue.text: The state of Ontario water?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, a part of them

explanation.surface: Asks about the condition of the water in Ontario, a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The state of' reads as 'the condition of'; really 'The state' is the definition and 'of' takes letters out of 'Ontario water'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state, so it fits a definition naming a state of the Union.

clue.text: Appreciation of view expressed by King George?

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: spoken, so the word for a view is given by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: an attitude is a view or opinion

explanation.surface: Wonders how King George phrased his opinion of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: GR followed by the sound of ATTITUDE gives a word that sounds like it but drops one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thankfulness for a kindness received is appreciation of it.

clue.text: Complaint over duke's meal

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a beef is a gripe or complaint
the Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a duke's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of fillet steak baked in pastry, served as a main course.

clue.text: Offending Labour Party?

parts.note: not an insult to the political party but a work party made up of offenders

explanation.surface: Sounds like a headline about someone upsetting the British Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour Party' looks like the British political party; read it as a party (group) doing labour, made up of convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners shackled together and set to hard work form a labouring group of offenders.

clue.text: Wind breaker covering end of shore

indicators.note: the breaker goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

indicators.note: the final letter of the word shore

explanation.surface: Something that breaks the wind shelters the edge of the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind breaker' suggests a windbreak; 'Wind' is the definition, the verb to wind, as a road does.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind or zigzag along a path is to move in and out, as a road does through hills.

clue.text: Makes an inventory first, in case of ladies

indicators.note: the ordinal goes inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: 1st, written IST

explanation.surface: Someone cataloguing items starts with a ladies' suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To list goods is to write them down one by one, which is drawing up an inventory.

clue.text: Particular about kite mark? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: normally means going round something, here the definition going round the words
flips the relation, so the words go round the definition and contain it

explanation.surface: A detail concerning the Kitemark, the British product-safety logo, but the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, 'Particular about kite mark' puts the answer round the words; 'Quite the reverse' means the words 'kite mark' hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a particular is a single detail or point, one entry in a list.

clue.text: Suitable returns following argument

indicators.note: the word for suitable comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: fit means suitable
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Something fitting comes back after a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a small falling-out between friends.

clue.text: Worker trapped by wild pig with a bear?

indicators.note: the worker is caught inside the scrambled letters
letters running wild are rearranged

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
and means together with

explanation.surface: An employee is cornered by a wild boar, and then a bear turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white Chinese animal is classified among the bear family.

clue.text: Argued about accepting quiet promotion

indicators.note: taking the letter into the middle of the shuffled word
the letters are turned about, put in a new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone protested about quietly being given a better job.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving up to a higher grade or rank at work is a promotion.

clue.text: Mostly neglectful — reforming to show respect

indicators.note: forming the letters anew, an arrangement
most of the word, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A careless person is mending their ways to show some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last L to give NEGLECTFU, and 'reforming' rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the knee, as in church or before royalty, is a gesture of reverence.

clue.text: Respect excursion being cut short — only right of course

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
but means only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: the rightmost, last, letter of the word course

explanation.surface: A trip cut short, out of respect, keeping only to the right of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is a mark of esteem or honour paid to someone.

clue.text: Watches people after game

definitions.meaning: pocket watches with hinged metal covers over the face are called by this name
those who pursue wild animals for sport

explanation.surface: Spectators keep an eye on people after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a verb and 'game' like a match; one is the timepiece, the other quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch with a protective lid, and also one who chases game.

clue.text: Turn bad, as a follow-up TV series might be

definitions.text: as a follow-up TV series might be

parts.note: to spin is to turn round
food that has gone off is bad

explanation.surface: Going sour, as a sequel series often does.
explanation.definitionFit: A show derived from an earlier hit, built around one of its characters, is described with this term.

clue.text: Hide from company and clean building

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new structure, rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm conceals something from another company and a newly cleaned building.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to keep it out of sight, to cover it up.

clue.text: Mysterious tomb — Inca, oddly

parts.note: a crypt is an underground tomb

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: An Inca burial chamber full of mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure in meaning, puzzling and enigmatic, like these crosswords.

clue.text: Runs to the rear platform on water

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
aft means towards the stern or back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone dashes to the back of a floating platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat structure of logs or planks that floats is a simple platform for use on water.

clue.text: Shame! Mine's the fourth of July!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine; the 's is 'has' joining the pieces

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Independence Day falls on someone else's watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fourth of July' looks like American Independence Day; here it is just the fourth letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'What a pity!' expresses regret, much like 'What a shame!'

clue.text: Nut is capable of going after exercise

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A nutty person who is able to go after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is the edible nut of a hickory tree from North America.

clue.text: Some music that may strike one as familiar

definitions.meaning: a group of notes sounded together is a piece of music

definitions.text: that may strike one as familiar
definitions.meaning: from the idiom of striking a ..., something resonating as recognisable

explanation.surface: A tune that feels like you have heard it before.
explanation.walkthrough: Something that feels familiar is said to strike a chord; the notes themselves are also struck together on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes played at once form a bit of harmony, and the idiom ties the same word to recognition.

clue.text: Slowness to act to screen a covered walkway

indicators.note: the words screen, hide away, the letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone is slow to put up a screen along a covered path.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a portico or roofed colonnade was a public covered walk.

clue.text: Nice surprise for soldiers surrounded by rubbish?

indicators.note: the soldiers go inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbishy goods
RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A pleasant surprise for troops stuck among junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special pleasure or unexpected delight given to someone.

clue.text: Not joining in work can get initially unpopular

parts.note: OP is opus, a musical work
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the first letter of the word get

parts.note: out means out of favour, no longer fashionable

explanation.surface: A worker refusing to join in could become unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb (is able); it is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing to withdraw from a scheme or group is declining to take part.

clue.text: Official warned off after dealing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the word for dealing

parts.note: to traffic is to deal in goods, often illicitly

indicators.note: the letters are off, out of their proper order

explanation.surface: An official issued a warning after catching someone dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRAFFIC WARDEN in Britain is a uniformed official who enforces parking rules and issues tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed parking enforcer employed by a council is a minor public official.
